newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 0.50 to 1.00 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 0.50 to 1.00 lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 0.50 to 1.00 cent lower Friday, although dealers expect the market to trade quietly ahead of the release of Green Coffee Association of New York's monthly stock report after today's close.

Most industry sources expect the data to show a fairly modest build in U.S. green coffee inventories during July. Industry estimates have called for an increase of 50,000 to 150,000 60-kg bags, although some dealers predicted a stock build of up to 250,000 bags.

Thursday, New York arabicas ended mixed in dull trading, with spot September settling up 1.45 cents at 184.55 cents a lb after ranging from 186.75 to 180.00 cents. Active December finished up 0.55 cent at 166.05 cents, while the back months closed down 0.10 to 0.60 cent.
The September/December switch widened to 18.50 cents compared with 17.60 cents at the close on Tuesday. December/March 1998 stretched to 16.85 cents versus 16.20 cents the previous session.
Technically, traders pegged September support at 180.00 cents, then 177.50 cents and 175.00 cents. Resistance was seen at 187.00 cents, followed by 188.50 cents and 191.50 cents.

On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Friday that no damaging cold weather is expected during the next seven days in Brazil's coffee belt, with temperatures near to above normal levels.

After Thursday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 839 60-kg bags as of August 13, to 92,120 bags. There were an additional 5,800 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.

London robusta futures were mixed in thin, switch-dominated trade early Friday. LIFFE September was unchanged at the midday break, to $1,515, after ranging from $1,527 to $1,510. November was up $1, to $1,531.
The London exchange said on Friday that LIFFE certified coffee stocks rose to 4,657 five-tonne lots in July from 2,346 lots in June. This was marginally higher than expectations, traders there said.
